title: Tanzanian Fish Tamarind Stew
author: Chef Fatuma
desc: Tanzanian Mchuzi wa Samaki wa Ukwaju — fish stew with tamarind, coconut milk, and Zanzibar spices. The sweet-sour-spiced fish stew of the coastal kitchen — tamarind and coconut milk creating a uniquely complex sauce.
longDesc: This fish stew combines tamarind's tartness with coconut milk richness and Zanzibar spices for extraordinary complexity. It uses the coastal Tanzanian pantry most completely.
steps: Season fish with salt and turmeric.
Cook onions until golden. Add garlic, ginger, spices.
Add coconut milk and tamarind. Stir to combine.
Bring to gentle simmer. Add fish. Cover and simmer gently 10—12 minutes.
Adjust sweet-sour balance with sugar. Garnish with coriander.
chefTips: Balance tamarind tartness with sugar to taste.
cookingScience: Tamarind's tartaric acid and coconut milk fats create an emulsified sauce — acid prevents fat separation while fat rounds the acidity's sharpness.
sustainabilityTips: Tamarind and coconut from coastal Tanzanian trees.
culturalNote: The combination of tamarind and coconut milk in a fish stew is the signature of the Swahili coast — Arab-introduced tamarind and the African coconut palm creating something that belongs entirely to Tanzania.
